decisions.reason: As a close-to-core data archiving and reporting software product that fits the firm's data-driven trajectory, its survival past the initial launch period suggests results are at least near aspiration, so management would keep it.

Despite weaker web prominence, it is still close to the established software offer and in a growing, innovative firm with some slack it would usually be retained unless performance had clearly fallen below aspiration.

This safety-related hardware complement is less central to the firm's digital direction, but it still supports integrated infrastructure projects and is more likely to be kept than dropped absent clear evidence of persistent underperformance.

Control technology for water engineering machinery sits in the core of the firm's systems business, so boundedly rational management would continue it and tolerate normal uncertainty rather than withdraw it.

Flow measurement automation and system software aligns strongly with the firm's connected and predictive infrastructure strategy, and after the early learning phase it is likely to remain above aspiration or worth supporting with available slack.
